description: NASA Disasters Mapping Portal is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by NASA Earth Science Disasters Program; NASA Applied Sciences Program. This site promotes the use of Earth observations to improve prediction of, preparation for, response to, and recovery from natural and technological disasters. The portal provides information and maps to support disaster response and recovery. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Flooding – Rainfall-induced, High Winds, Severe Winter Weather, Wildfire. Assets: Natural Areas and Wildlife, People, Property. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
